answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a scarce, verifiable resource instead of free registration: an agent must stake a deposit or prove sustained useful work before it can transact. Fake identities then become expensive to mass-produce, while honest agents earn reputation over time. Like an island community guarding its nectar, the network lets trust echo through referrals from established participants, so a newcomer is vouched for by someone with skin in the game rather than self-asserting.
